changes: Registered-project recovery/list and recovery/read expose bounded fixed-slot versions and manifests. Browser paths never come from native-owned journals.

Durable recovery/restore copies an exact selected backup into an explicit scoped destination, checks both revisions and captures replaced content. Source backups remain available; absent destinations use no-replace rename.

Durable recovery/discard requires confirmation/current manifest and completed source state, captures and rechecks all selected payloads before deletion, preserves the original receipt and uses a small cleanup reservation. Unknown/failed sources cannot be discarded.

Gateway methods, receipt minimization, ledger reconciliation and supervisor-private witness bind restore/discard identities. Witness completion additionally matches reserved project/root/helper digest/gateway digest/current operation.
Affected-test mapping pairs workspace and recovery fixtures and retains all three ordinary/root provider-layer fixture files.

tests.command: node scripts/run-tests.mjs --targeted tests/runtime/workspace.test.ts tests/runtime/workspace-witness.test.ts tests/gateway/receipt-result.test.ts tests/gateway/dispatch.test.ts

tests.coverage: Real descriptor and renameat2 operations, file/directory/binary recovery, source/target revision conflicts, explicit path scope, publish/capture races, byte-pressure discard, receipt replay, unknown-state preservation, project isolation, prior file/Git regressions.

testCorrections: Initial tooling run lacked HARNESS_TEST_PYTHON and could not run its interpreter fixture; rerun with the exact authorized executable passed all 23 assertions. No platform gap was reported as passing.
limits: No live service changes, full suite, external MCP or paid inference. Linux run used only native-owned temporary fixture paths.
Receipt identities remain bounded to 256 per project; explicit payload discard frees bytes but does not reset operation IDs or remove unknown records.
Web UI is integrated by a separate agent. Worktree lifecycle is a separate subsequent module, not claimed complete here.
Separate follow-up identified repository clean filters executed by Git status/diff; those queries require a further isolated Git-view hardening change before final acceptance.
